req.title: /status/<code> accepts POST
req.statement: The system shall accept POST requests on /status/<code> and return the requested code.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /status/<code> must return the requested HTTP status code. I design tests covering: (1) a standard 2xx positive case (200), (2) a negative/client-error case (400), (3) boundary cases at the edges of common status code ranges (100, 299, 300, 500), (4) an invalid code negative path, and (5) a 5xx server-error code. Each test asserts the exact status code to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations. Tests also verify that the endpoint rejects non-POST methods where appropriate and that the route is registered for POST.

tests.name: test_post_status_method_not_allowed_on_get_only_route
actions: Send GET request to /status/200 to confirm GET also works
Send POST to /status/201 to confirm POST is accepted
trace: R-HTTPBIN-046: NEG — confirms POST is explicitly allowed (not 405); catches method-list mutation
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_status_method_not_allowed_on_get_only_route():
    r_get = client.get('/status/200')
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    r_post = client.post('/status/201')
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    assert r_post.status_code != 405

test_post_status_method_not_allowed_on_get_only_route()
